name: Anterior approach to the capitellum
corridor: Between brachioradialis and brachialis after identification and mobilization of the radial nerve

positioning.text: Position supine with arm on a hand table, elbow extendable, and forearm rotatable for nerve protection and imaging.

setup.text: Confirm by CT that posterior capitellar comminution is absent and prepare magnification and vessel-loop control of the radial nerve and branches.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark biceps lateral border, brachioradialis medial border, elbow crease, radial head, and lateral epicondyle.

incision.text: Use a curved anterior incision from the lateral biceps border proximally toward the medial brachioradialis border distally.

superficial_interval.text: Open biceps fascia, retract biceps medially, and identify and protect the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve.

deep_interval.text: Develop brachioradialis-brachialis interval, identify radial nerve, trace it to PIN and superficial branch, then retract muscles with nerve protected before longitudinal capsulotomy.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous sensory plane, biceps fascia, brachialis-brachioradialis interval, radial-nerve plane, capsule, then capitellum.

structures_encountered.text: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve, biceps, brachialis, brachioradialis, radial nerve, PIN, superficial radial nerve, capsule, and capitellum are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Radial nerve and branches, lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve, brachial vessels medially, cartilage, and anterior capsule are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The radial nerve contacts capsule near the radial neck; avoid distal blind capsular dissection or prolonged anterior retraction.

retraction_hazards.text: Maintain direct nerve visualization and use broad intermittent retraction; do not lever over the radial head or neck.

exposure.text: Exposes anterior capitellum and lateral trochlear ridge with direct anterior-to-posterior fixation access.

limitations.text: Cannot visualize posterior capitellum and is unsuitable for posterior comminution or complex trochlear extension.

extensions.text: Convert to a lateral/extensile approach if posterior reduction cannot be assessed rather than extending blindly around the radial nerve.

indications.text: Use for simple anterior capitellar shear fractures without posterior comminution.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid for posterior comminution, complex trochlear extension, or when radial-nerve mobilization is unsafe.

implant_implications.text: Allows perpendicular anterior fixation; countersink headless screws and confirm posterior exit and joint containment.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, oblique, and radiocapitellar views to confirm reduction, screw trajectory, and absence of posterior prominence.

closure.text: Repair capsule, release retractors and confirm radial-nerve continuity, then close fascia and skin in layers.

complications.text: Complications include radial/PIN palsy, sensory nerve injury, stiffness, fixation failure, avascular necrosis, heterotopic ossification, and arthritis.

bailouts.text: Convert to lateral exposure when posterior comminution is found or radial-nerve-safe visualization is inadequate.

procedure_applications.condition: A simple anterior capitellar fracture without posterior comminution requires direct anterior reduction and screw fixation

questions.question: What fracture pattern is appropriate?
questions.answer: A simple capitellar fracture without posterior comminution.

questions.question: Which nerve must be traced to its branches?
questions.answer: The radial nerve to PIN and superficial radial nerve.
